claimed.text: Inventories published by others describe Release 01 as 160 files (117 PDFs, 29 sensor videos, 14 photographs) spanning 1944 to 2026, at least 100 of them redacted, including Apollo 12 and 17 records and the FBI's master flying disc file for 1947 to 1968.

Release 02 is described as 64 files, 51 of them sensor videos, including an MQ-9 weapons-quality lock on an object showing instantaneous acceleration and spheres entering and leaving the water near a surfaced US submarine.

Release 03 is described as 72 files, 29 from the FBI, including an FBI orb corpus from 2021 to 2025 with two agents' own first-hand report, a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel report and a 2008 CIA file on a disc over Harare airport.
Release 04 is described as including previously unseen military video and documents back to the 1940s, several of the videos assessed as consistent with balloons or sensor artefacts.

Release 05 is described as including six AC-130J videos of about 25 cold orbs over the Gulf of Oman in 2021 said to react to cannon fire, a 1953 Navy Photographic Interpretation Center finding that the Utah film objects were self-luminous and intelligently controlled, and a CIA report of a 1963 Brazil sphere with a dead occupant that the US consulate judged unsubstantiated.

DNI Gabbard called the first release an ongoing joint effort of the intelligence and defence agencies; Sean Parnell, the Secretary of War's public affairs assistant, said more files would follow on a rolling basis; Luna publicly thanked the President; and Senator Gillibrand said the administration had heard her call but still had to meet its legal obligation.
Officials described the July 2026 NDA waiver as not a declassification directive: it permits disclosure only to cleared investigators at AARO or the PURSUE task force.
The White House registered alien.gov and aliens.gov on 17 March 2026, and a spokeswoman replied only that people should stay tuned; neither domain was used for the releases.

contested.text: Christopher Mellon said data alone is not disclosure, Tim Gallaudet that missing metadata makes it impossible to conclude any object was anomalous, Alejandro Rojas that summaries without coordinates, sensor parameters or altitude block independent analysis, and Ryan Graves that ambiguous imagery without context cannot be evaluated responsibly.

The Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies found that Release 01 stripped time, date, location, range, altitude and speed, recycled about 70 percent of its FBI files from the existing Vault, contained nothing from DOE, DIA, NRO, NSA or CIA, and left a 1974 to 2015 gap. The metadata stripped is the obstacle NASA's study team had named.

Many PDFs were password-protected against text recognition until The Black Vault removed the restriction three days after Release 01; the board infers that the working public index is a private mirror, and that redactions carrying no exemption citations cannot be appealed through any existing mechanism.

The board infers that the programme rests on informal direction, leaving its scope discretionary; and the records disagree on when Hegseth called it that executive order, 23 February in one account and 25 February in another.

No charter, roster, budget or location for the PURSUE Task Force is public, on the board's reading. Burlison said it is unclear whether the NDA abrogation covers testimony given to Congress before referral, and the board infers that the waiver unbinds witnesses only inside the executive channel that failed Grusch.

Release 04 came with no file count, and a summary of its announcement characterised several videos as consistent with balloons or sensor artefacts, which the board reads as assessment language returning despite the no-comment posture and as the programme's accounting degrading.

The board reads PURSUE as a verdict on AARO: the Department released at cabinet direction the kind of material AARO had called unavailable, its FY2025 report never mentions the programme, and its declassification paper's account of a slow process was overturned in weeks.

Roughly sixteen gigabytes were released while AARO's promised Historical Record Report Volume II stayed unpublished, and the FY2024 report blamed a lack of sensor data nineteen months before one tranche published 51 sensor videos of earlier incidents. The board also notes that the 2021 Gulf of Oman engagement appears in neither AARO annual report that covers its date.

lead.text: PURSUE is the Department of War's programme for releasing government UAP files, begun on a presidential direction in February 2026 and published in five tranches at war.gov/UFO between 8 May and 7 August 2026. The Department attaches no comment or assessment to any file, and critics say that without metadata the releases cannot be evaluated.

record.text: The portal lists Release 01 on 8 May 2026 with 1.2GB of documents and 1.3GB of video; Release 02 on 22 May with 70.1MB and 5.6GB; Release 03 on 12 June with 826MB and 4.6GB; Release 04 on 10 July with 227MB and 1.4GB; and Release 05 on 7 August with 130MB and 513MB.
The portal gives only a date and two bundle sizes per release, serves video from a CloudFront distribution, and carries no FOIA case numbers or exemption citations.

A War Department official stated that the Department is providing no comment or assessment on the files overall or any single file, so that the public can make up its own mind. Hegseth's portal statement says the Department is in lockstep with the President on transparency, and the Department says it will continue separate statutory reporting on resolved cases.

Release 05 holds 41 files: 16 videos, 22 documents and 3 images. Its identifiers include the Gulf of Oman gunship video and intelligence report of September 2021, a 1953 analysis of the Montana and Utah films, an FBI report of a triangle near Colorado Springs in October 2023, and a November 1963 Brazil diplomatic cable and incident report under DOS and EOP prefixes.

ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818, signed by Principal Deputy DNI Aaron Lukas, directs release of all intelligence community UAP information to the PURSUE Task Force for review and declassification. Every element must name a PURSUE designee within 30 days and tell its workforce that NDAs barring disclosure to the President or designees like PURSUE are no longer in force; the distribution runs from CIA, DIA, NGA, NRO, NSA and the FBI to DOE and every service intelligence chief.

Release 02 published, under an ODNI document number, a serving officer's first-person narrative of a one-hour, multi-witness encounter; and infrared video of the February 2023 Lake Huron shootdown came out through PURSUE on 22 May 2026.

Luna wrote to the Secretary of War for AARO's UAP video holdings (one record dates the letter 31 March 2026, another 1 April) after witnesses told her task force AARO held more records; the first PURSUE tranche followed within five weeks.

Rep. Eric Burlison welcomed the NDA waiver as something he had called for, offered his office as a channel and advised witnesses to ask for congressional presence and counsel. He published the ODNI memorandum on 1 August 2026, sent MITRE a records demand on 22 May 2026 framed as enforcing records identified for public release, and authored the disclosure amendment the House adopted in July 2026, which creates a review board with subpoena power and contractor disclosure obligations.
The FBI, largest single contributor to Release 03, is also a contributor to the National Archives UAP record group, while its own public Vault collection has not been modified since July 2013.

summary.text: The programme stands on President Trump's Truth Social post of 19 to 20 February 2026 saying he would direct Hegseth and other departments to begin identifying and releasing files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. No executive order has been published, and ODNI's implementing memo cites only presidential direction.

The Department of War runs it with ODNI support, and AARO identifies and stages the material; but the files are published on the Secretary of War's website, not AARO's, and AARO's own homepage simply links to it.
Each of the five tranches, dated 8 May, 22 May, 12 June, 10 July and 7 August 2026, is a paired document bundle and video bundle.

Around the releases sits a second track: an ODNI memorandum naming a PURSUE Task Force with review and declassification authority, and a July 2026 presidential direction waiving UAP-related non-disclosure agreements for people who speak to AARO or PURSUE investigators.
